subject: KMS interop & TLS cipher-suite mapping for SafeHarbor RFP
messages:
From: Adam Blake <adam.blake@safeharborhealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: SafeHarbor Security <security@safeharborhealth.com>, procurement@safeharborhealth.com
Date: 2027-08-08T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: KMS and TLS mapping questions for Redwood — SafeHarbor RFP #SH-2027-21

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the materials so far. Our security team has a few technical clarifications we need before we can progress to the PBSA and procurement stage. I attached a spreadsheet of the items that need explicit answers, but high-level asks below: 

1) BYOK: what import methods do you support for customer KEKs and DEKs? Specifically: KMIP key import (with explicit wrapped key formats), PKCS#12, and RSA/OAEP-wrapped imports. Can keys be imported such that SafeHarbor retains sole possession of the unwrapped material?

2) HSM certs & attestation: do you use FIPS 140-2/3 validated HSMs in production? Can you provide attestation artifacts (module certificate number, vendor, operation mode)?

3) Key lifecycle: what rotation operations are exposed via API vs manual? Can we schedule automatic KEK rotation without re-encrypting object-store data immediately (i.e., support for lazy rewrap)?

4) TLS & ciphers: we require TLS configuration details for your inference endpoints and control plane. We prefer TLS 1.3 only, plus a mapping of allowed cipher suites for mTLS client auth. Please confirm supported curves and server cipher order.

5) Audit & evidence: retention window for KMS audit logs, format (immutable ledger, or regular logs), and how to access them for audit requests.

If you can provide short answers and point us to the specific evidence artifacts (or attach them), that would be ideal. We are hoping to complete evaluations by 8/20.

Best,
Adam
Adam Blake
Technical PM, SafeHarbor Healthcare

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Adam Blake <adam.blake@safeharborhealth.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-08T11:04:00-04:00
Subject: Re: KMS and TLS mapping questions for Redwood — SafeHarbor RFP #SH-2027-21

Adam — thank you, quick answers inline below and I've attached a compact matrix and our BYOK onboarding playbook for the procurement and security teams. Happy to jump on a call if you prefer.

On 2027-08-08 at 09:12 AM Adam Blake <adam.blake@safeharborhealth.com> wrote:
> 1) BYOK import methods? Sole possession?

- Supported import methods: KMIP (1.4) wrapped key import (RFC 6030 variants), PKCS#12 import for certificate/private-key bundles (encrypted with password you provide), and AES-KWP (RFC 5649) / RSA-OAEP wrapped key import for KEKs.
- Sole possession: Yes — we support customer-controlled key material import where the unwrapped key never leaves customer control. Options: (a) wrapped import using your public RSA key or (b) client-side envelope encryption prior to upload. When using our BYOK flow the wrapped material is delivered to an HSM-backed import endpoint; Redwood does not retain an unencrypted copy. Details in attached playbook (redwood-byo-onboarding-playbook.pdf).

> 2) HSM FIPS & attestation?

- Production HSMs: We run FIPS 140-2 Level 2/3 validated modules depending on cloud region/vendor (AWS CloudHSM for hosted, Thales Luna/FIPS module for Dedicated clusters if requested). Attestation artifacts: we can provide module certificate numbers and vendor attestations under NDA.

> 3) Key rotation APIs and lazy rewrap?

- Rotation operations: KEK rotation and rewrap are exposed via the KMS Admin API (rotate-key, schedule-rotation, start-rewrap).
- Lazy rewrap: supported. You can rotate KEKs (generate new KEK and set it primary) without forcing immediate re-encryption of objects; objects are rewrapped on access or via batch rewrap jobs. We document rewrap semantics and have rewrap operators to control concurrency and throughput.

> 4) TLS & cipher support

- Control plane (API) endpoints: TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 supported; by default we enable TLS 1.3 only for new tenants. Cipher suites: for TLS1.3 we support the standard AEAD suites (TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256). For TLS1.2 we support ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 and ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384; we prioritize server cipher order and prefer ECDHE + AEAD. Curves: X25519, secp256r1 (P-256). mTLS: supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; you can upload client certs or integrate with our CA. Details in the matrix.

> 5) Audit logs

- Audit retention: default 90 days; enterprise options up to 7 years (archival).
- Format & access: immutable audit ledger for KMS events (signed logs + append-only store) with export as newline-delimited JSON; access via our audit API or S3 export. Query-by-key-id, time-range, and action-type is supported.

Next steps: I attached "redwood-kms-tls-matrix.xlsx" mapping the items in your sheet to answers and evidence links. If the security team wants attestation artifacts we can share module certs and a short attestation package; I'm copying Irene from Security to coordinate access.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0198

Subject: Re: KMS and TLS mapping questions for Redwood — SafeHarbor RFP #SH-2027-21

Lauren — quick clarifications after reviewing the matrix: 

- For BYOK imports, can you confirm support for RSA-OAEP-256 (RSAES-OAEP with SHA-256) wrapped KEK imports? Our HSM provisioning tool only outputs OAEP-256-wrapped material.
- For lazy rewrap, will the rewrap operation preserve object metadata and versioning so our storage access patterns are not impacted? We want to avoid extra object churn during rotation windows.
- For endpoint TLS: we require TLS 1.3-only for inference traffic in our production environment. Can you provide a network-level config doc or guidance for forcing TLS1.3-only for our tenant?

If possible, please attach any sample API calls for rotate-key and the rewrap-job API.

Thanks,
Adam

From: irene_choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Adam Blake <adam.blake@safeharborhealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-09T17:22:00-04:00
Subject: Re: KMS and TLS mapping questions for Redwood — SafeHarbor RFP #SH-2027-21

Adam — hi, Irene from Security. Quick answers and links below, attaching a short sample snippet for rotate-key and rewrap-job.

- RSA-OAEP-256: supported. Our import endpoint accepts RSAES-OAEP with SHA-256 mask generation (OAEP-256) and we validate OAEP parameters. We also support AES-KWP and raw KMIP wrapped imports.

- Lazy rewrap semantics: rewrap preserves object metadata and version history. Rewrap is applied to the object envelope (DEK wrapped under current KEK) without creating new object IDs; if you use object-store-level immutability we will honor the semantics and provide rewrap-aside jobs that operate on copies only when requested. We document safe windows and throttling controls.

- TLS1.3-only: we can enforce TLS 1.3-only for tenant ingress in hosted or Dedicated via tenant-level policy. We'll provide a tenant config snippet (attached) and can schedule a short cutover with networking if you want to test in staging first.

- Evidence & attestation: per our standard process we can provide: HSM module cert numbers, vendor attestations, and a short whitepaper on our import endpoint design under NDA. For SOC2 / ISO artifacts, we will provide redacted copies via a secure share; procurement, please confirm NDA route.

Attached: sample-apis.txt (rotate-key / rewrap-job examples), tenant-tls-config-snippet.txt, attestation-request-form.pdf

If useful, Karhith (cc'd) and Lauren can run a short technical session to demo a wrapped-key import and rewrap run.

Best,
Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

Attachments: sample-apis.txt, tenant-tls-config-snippet.txt, attestation-request-form.pdf
